stem.en: Why do picture models do their work on latent codes instead of pixels?

text.en: Any random latent code opens into a good picture.
Each latent code stores a small copy of a training picture.
The numbers in a latent code have names a model can read.
A latent code has far fewer numbers, so work is cheaper.

explanation.en: A latent code holds the picture in 48 times fewer numbers, and the decoder handles the fine detail. Random latent codes open into speckle, as you saw. A latent code is worked out for one picture and is no copy from a pile, and its numbers have no names.
